sources.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust: a Better `ls` with clap, tabled and serde

steps.title: Create project and parse arguments
steps.instructions: Run `cargo new best_ls`, add clap with the derive feature, and define a `Cli` struct deriving `Parser` with `path: Option<PathBuf>` in src/main.rs. Call `Cli::parse()` in main and run `cargo run -- -h` to see the generated help.

explanations.topic: Adding clap with the derive feature
Using -- to pass arguments to cargo run

hints: Which trait has to be derived for your struct to get a `parse()` method?
Add `#[derive(Parser)]` and `use clap::Parser;`, and make sure Cargo.toml enables `features = ["derive"]`.
In Cargo.toml write `clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] }`, then run `cargo run -- -h`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the `derive` feature on clap, so `#[derive(Parser)]` fails to compile
Running `cargo run -h`, which shows cargo's help instead of your program's
Not importing `std::path::PathBuf`

steps.title: Add version and about metadata
steps.instructions: Annotate `Cli` with `#[command(version, about, long_about = "best ls command ever")]`. Run it with `--version` and then with `-h`.

targets.caption: Text shown in the long help

explanations.topic: long_about shown in the help output

hints: clap reads extra CLI metadata from an attribute placed above the struct.
Use `#[command(...)]` and list `version` and `about` inside it.
`#[command(version, about, long_about = "best ls command ever")]`
common_mistakes: Using `#[clap(...)]` from older tutorials instead of `#[command(...)]`
Putting the attribute on the field instead of the struct

steps.title: Read path with default fallback
steps.instructions: Set `let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from("."));` and print `path.display()`. Run once with `long_path` and once without an argument.

explanations.topic: Option path defaults to '.' when no argument is given

hints: `cli.path` is an Option, so what do you want to happen when it is None?
Use `unwrap_or` and give it a `PathBuf` that points to the current directory.
`let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from("."));` followed by `println!("{}", path.display());`
common_mistakes: Printing a PathBuf with `{}` directly instead of using `.display()`
Using `unwrap()`, which panics when no path is given

steps.title: Handle missing paths in red
steps.instructions: Match on `fs::exists(&path)` and print "Path does not exist" in red with owo-colors when missing, or "Error reading directory" if it cannot be checked.

targets.caption: Branch on whether the path exists

explanations.topic: exists returns Ok only if existence can be verified
Running the debug binary from target/debug

hints: The existence check returns a Result<bool>, so you need two layers of branching.
Use `if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path)` and then branch on `does_exist`.
Add owo-colors, `use owo_colors::OwoColorize;`, then `println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red());`
common_mistakes: Forgetting `use owo_colors::OwoColorize;`, so `.red()` is not found
Ignoring the Err case of the existence check

steps.title: List directory file names
steps.instructions: Write `fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String>` using `fs::read_dir`, pushing each entry's file name. Loop over it in main and print each name, then run `cargo run`.

explanations.topic: Iterating read_dir entries, each of which is a Result

hints: Which std::fs function returns an iterator over a directory's entries?
`fs::read_dir(path)` gives a Result of entries, and each entry is also a Result.
Push `file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())` into a Vec and return it.
common_mistakes: Passing `path` instead of `&path` to get_files
Forgetting that file_name() returns an OsString, which needs into_string()

steps.title: Collect file metadata into structs
steps.instructions: Define `FileEntry` (name, e_type, len_bytes, modified) and `EntryType` (File, Dir) deriving strum's `Display`, fill them from `fs::metadata` in `map_data`, and debug-print the Vec.

explanations.topic: Enum for file vs directory type
strum Display derive for printing enums
Bug: metadata must use file.path(), not the dir path

hints: The metadata has to come from the entry itself, not from the directory you are listing.
Use `fs::metadata(&file.path())` and check `meta.is_dir()` to decide the type.
Set `len_bytes: meta.len()` and debug-print with `{:#?}` or `{:?}`.
common_mistakes: Calling `fs::metadata(path)` on the parent directory, so every row shows the same data
Naming a field `type`, which is a reserved keyword (use `e_type`)
Forgetting `use strum::Display;`

steps.title: Render a coloured table
steps.instructions: Derive `Tabled` on FileEntry, build `Table::new(get_files(&path))` with `Style::rounded()`, colour columns and the header row, and rename headers with `#[tabled(rename = ...)]`.

explanations.topic: tabled crate prints structs as an ASCII table

hints: The struct needs one more derive before Table::new will accept it.
Add `Tabled` to the derive list, then `let mut table = Table::new(get_files(&path));`.
Use `table.with(Style::rounded())` and `table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN)`.
common_mistakes: Not deriving Tabled on FileEntry (and leaving EntryType without Display)
Forgetting `let mut` on the table before calling with/modify
Enabling colours without the `ansi` feature of tabled

steps.title: Format modified date with chrono
steps.instructions: In map_data, convert `meta.modified()` into `DateTime<Utc>` and format it into `modified`, falling back to an empty string.

explanations.topic: modified() returns Result<SystemTime>; chrono converts it

hints: `meta.modified()` returns a Result, so handle both cases.
A SystemTime can be turned into a chrono `DateTime<Utc>` with `.into()`.
Write `let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into();` then `format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y"))`.
common_mistakes: Using `mod` as a variable name (it is a keyword)
Missing `use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};`
Omitting the type annotation, so `.into()` cannot infer DateTime<Utc>

steps.title: Add a --json output flag
steps.instructions: Add `#[arg(short, long)] json: bool` to Cli, derive `Serialize` on FileEntry and EntryType, and move the table into `print_table`. When `cli.json` is set print `serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path))`, then run `cargo run -- -j`.

explanations.topic: clap arg with short and long variants
serde Serialize + serde_json for JSON output

hints: A bool field in Cli only becomes a flag once you give it an `#[arg]` attribute.
Use `#[arg(short, long)]` so both -j and --json work, and derive `Serialize` on both types.
`println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path)).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string()));`
common_mistakes: Deriving Serialize on FileEntry but not on EntryType
Adding serde without the `derive` feature
Using `cli.path` after moving it into `path`, which causes a borrow/move error
